$comment: Connection profiles for the UniFi Protect POS ingestion POC. No secrets here: the API key lives in the SecretManagement vault named below. Switch target by changing activeProfile, or pass -ProfileName to any script. One profile per console: the integration APIs are LAN-only, so each console needs its own key and its own reachable address.

lawson.$comment: Lawson, UDM-PRO-SE, MAC 60:22:32:13:4D:E9. This is the console from design.md and the one reachable at 192.168.1.1 from the dev machine. Self-signed cert, hence skipCertificateCheck (the equivalent of curl -k). Verified 18 Oct 2026: UniFi OS 5.1.132, Network 10.6.106, Protect 7.3.70.

$template.$comment: Copy this block, rename it to the console name, and fill in the LAN address to add another site. Each console issues its own API key, so give each one a distinct secretName and store it with Initialize-UnifiSecret.ps1 -ProfileName <name>.

$cloudNote: There is deliberately no cloud profile. Verified 18 Oct 2026: https://unifi.ui.com/proxy/consoles/<id>/... returns HTTP 302 to account.ui.com/login when given X-API-KEY, because that path is browser-SSO only. The Site Manager API at api.ui.com DOES accept an X-API-KEY cloud key, but it exposes only read-only fleet inventory (hosts, sites, devices), not the Protect or Network integration APIs. For off-site access use a VPN or UniFi Teleport into the site LAN.

pos.$comment: POS ingestion settings. cameraId is filled in after running Get-UnifiCameras.ps1. alarmTriggerId is only used by the alarm-manager fallback transport.
